newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi stock market turnover jumps in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Saudi stock market turnover jumps in first quarter.

text.p: Over 83 million shares worth 12.06 billion riyals ($3.2 billion) were traded on the Saudi stock market in the first quarter of 1997, figures in the latest Saudi Arabian Monetary Agency (SAMA) bulletin show.
Turnover was considerably higher than in the first three months of last year, when 20.05 million shares worth almost 3.3 billion riyals were traded.

SAMA figures show that shares in the services sector were the most heavily traded in first quarter 1997, with over 40.2 million shares changing hands. Industrials and banks followed with a respective 12.09 million and 11.86 million shares traded.
In terms of value, banks led the way, with shares worth 3.78 billion riyals dealt. Services stocks came next with shares worth 3.09 billion riyals traded.
During 1996, over 137.83 million shares worth more than 25 billion riyals were traded. ($ = 3.750 Saudi Arabian Riyals)
